caption: Layer-wise norm differences from -1 to -5.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the relationship between “LLM layer index” and “Layerwise norm difference” for five different values of ‘c’. The y-axis, labeled “Layerwise norm difference”, is linear, ranging from 0.6 to 1.0 with tick marks at 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, and 1.0.  A red line, representing c=1, begins at approximately 0.98 at an LLM layer index of 0, decreases to approximately 0.68 at an LLM layer index of 2, then fluctuates between approximately 0.71 and 0.82 before rising to approximately 0.95 at an LLM layer index of 14. An orange line, representing c=2, starts at approximately 0.95 at an LLM layer index of 0, decreases to approximately 0.66 at an LLM layer index of 2, and then rises to approximately 0.84 at an LLM layer index of 14. A yellow line, representing c=3, begins at approximately 0.94 at an LLM layer index of 0, decreases to approximately 0.72 at an LLM layer index of 2, and then rises to approximately 0.78 at an LLM layer index of 14.  A green line, representing c=4, starts at approximately 0.96 at an LLM layer index of 0, decreases to approximately 0.71 at an LLM layer index of 2, and then rises to approximately 0.74 at an LLM layer index of 14. A blue line, representing c=5, begins at approximately 0.97 at an LLM layer index of 0, decreases to approximately 0.69 at an LLM layer index of 2, then rises to approximately 0.83 at an LLM layer index of 14.
